title: Cardinality bound for a union
statement: Let $S_0,S_1\subseteq\beta$ and let $c_0,c_1$ be nonnegative integers. Write $n(S)$ for the natural-number cardinality of a set, with infinite sets assigned cardinality zero. If $n(S_0)\le 2^{c_0}$ and $n(S_1)\le 2^{c_1}$, then $n(S_0\cup S_1)\le 2^{1+\max(c_0,c_1)}$.
replaced:
Let $S_0, S_1$ be sets in a type $\beta$ and let $c_0, c_1 \in \mathbb{N}$. If
$\abs{S_0} \le 2^{c_0}$ and $\abs{S_1} \le 2^{c_1}$, then
\[
  \abs{S_0 \cup S_1} \;\le\; 2^{\,1 + \max(c_0, c_1)},
\]
where $\abs{\cdot}$ denotes the number of elements of a set.
